purpose: Repair outcome-blind transport observability after the immutable R1 NOT_EVALUABLE terminal. This contract does not authorize network access, payload extraction, RGB decoding, RGB algorithm execution, Android work, source replacement, window replacement, or an R1 retry.

proven: The consumed R1 claim ended with INVALID_IDENTITY_EXTRACTION_CLOSE_ATTEMPT and error_type URLError.
Zero payload files, zero decodes, and zero RGB algorithm calls were produced.
The R1 transport retried a requested range at most three times before rethrowing URLError.
The failure occurred during a long-running solid-7z extraction context, not as a proven archive-format, memory, or RGB failure.
unknown: The failed range, phase, accumulated successful bytes, URLError reason class, and resource peak were not preserved.
The failure cannot be classified as DNS, TLS, proxy, timeout, reset, HTTP-layer, or resource-pressure-related from R1 evidence.
r2_required_observability: Append-only per-attempt range ledger with logical request id, phase, start, end, requested bytes, attempt, monotonic timestamps, sanitized status, HTTP status, Content-Range, successful bytes, and accounted bytes.
Sanitized exception taxonomy and exception-chain hash without URL query, credentials, headers, response bodies, or proxy secrets.
Failure receipt with real budget snapshot, last-good offset, last request, current phase, and peak RSS/commit.
Phase markers for archive header, directory, solid-folder pack, and target emission.
Terminal progress must preserve the last real snapshot and must not overwrite it with synthetic 0/1 progress.

proven: The ZIP member compressed-data start is outer byte 5626409670.
R1 read 1065353216 compressed member bytes through outer byte 6691762885, equal to 29.3215 percent of the member compressed bytes.
The stop occurred before the next network request because size-plus-one preauthorization exceeded the remaining R1 byte budget.
R1 did not identify a qualifying color connection and selected zero RGB frames.
unknown: No ROS bag record, topic, timestamp, logical offset, DEFLATE restart point, or time upper bound is bound to the R1 compressed cutoff.
The target RGB connection and selected window may occur later, but existing metadata cannot prove their location.
R1 preserved neither DEFLATE state nor downloaded bytes, so it cannot be resumed from the compressed cutoff.
minimum_index_authority_requirements: A new scan must start at the exact member compressed-data start; direct mid-member or tail range decoding is forbidden without a previously verified checkpoint.

The index must bind compressed and uncompressed offsets, DEFLATE bit position and 32 KiB dictionary, ROS top-level records and chunks, connection topic/type inventory, per-connection time range, message offsets, last complete record, partial buffer length, and highest observed timestamp.
Indexing may parse identity and timing metadata but may not decode, display, retain, or execute RGB pixel payloads.
If transient access to serialized RGB payload bytes for skipping or hashing is not separately authorized, the DLR branch must remain NOT_EVALUABLE.

minimum_no_retry_full_member_hard_cap.retry_rule: Any retry that consumes the fixed hard cap before a complete index produces NOT_EVALUABLE. The cap may not be increased during or after the claim.

allowed_without_external_access: Implement structured transport failures and append-only diagnostic ledgers in a new R2 namespace.
Use mocked DNS, TLS, proxy, timeout, reset, HTTP error, incomplete-read, wrong-Content-Range, and attempt-one-through-three failure cases.
Use local synthetic solid-7z and DEFLATE-plus-ROS-record fixtures.
Run secret scanning, budget property tests, deterministic receipt tests, and crash-safe append tests.
forbidden_without_later_signed_activatio: Any request to the frozen OpenLORIS or DLR URLs.
Any extraction, decoding, display, or algorithm call on target RGB frames.
Any change to a source, capture, exact window, member, target frame, or guard definition.
Any retry, resume, mutation, or reinterpretation of an R1 claim.

common: All outcome-blind tests pass against the frozen R2 implementation and runtime hashes.
An independent reviewer signs the exact contract, implementation, tests, runtime, byte cap, exception taxonomy, legal terminals, and claim namespace.
A new exclusive one-shot R2 claim namespace is used.
No outcome access occurs before claim creation and activation verification.
openloris: Keep the R1 source, exact window, 302 targets, guard definitions, byte cap, and maximum attempts unchanged.
Authorize at most one new R2 claim only after the observability repair is independently reviewed.
dlr: First obtain separate index-only authority for the minimum no-retry full-member hard cap of 3633353305 bytes or present a verified source-native checkpoint/index.
The fixed cap includes no retry headroom. Any retry that exhausts it produces NOT_EVALUABLE and may not trigger a cap increase.
After index review, freeze one unique RGB connection, timestamp field, pairing rule, and guard rule before any exact-window payload extraction.
A DLR index claim and a later exact-window extraction claim must be distinct and independently activated.

claim_ceiling.maximum_conclusion: A reviewed R2 design may establish that a new one-shot transport claim is reviewable. It cannot establish RGB mechanism evidence, distinguish positive from below, establish generalization or performance, support product or safety conclusions, or authorize Android.
claim_ceiling.source_role_confounding: OpenLORIS-positive and DLR-below remain source-role confounded. Even a later successful extraction permits only segment-by-segment RGB-versus-geometry consistency checks.
